notes: Round 10 runs several tracks at once, each in its own worktree: M1 (land animals), M2 (water mobs), M3 (night mobs) and W's w3 (the game events W's first merge left out). D0's d0b (silverfish in stone, endermites from pearls, flying navigation) is merged (c0366f3a), and release 6 is built with PROTOCOL 11 (789f6d23). Never bump minecraft_net::PROTOCOL: the release step bumps it once when messages changed; if a commit changes a ToClient/ToServer message or the codec, add a line under '## Protocol' in the track log. Insert new match arms and list entries next to related ones, not at the end of lists, to keep merges small (E3-0 names the few positional lists that are appended). Record decisions in the track log. LOAD: builds run at -j 4 per slot to keep the laptop cool; never start a second cargo command, the game, or any other long CPU-heavy process. Keep to the brief: each section names the commit its file:line anchors come from, so re-check every anchor before editing; keep off the hooks the M briefs own and follow the cross-area overlaps (both in E3-0). E2's e2b (44d96765) and D0's d0b (c0366f3a) are merged, so every 'waits for e2b', 'after d0b' and 'release 6 built' in the brief is met; d0b moved lines in server.rs, world.rs, walk_path.rs, entity_view.rs and families.rs, so anchors taken before it need a re-check. The orchestrator brings track-e3 up to minecraft-survival before each segment, so the review uses git diff r10-e3u-base..HEAD as usual. SEGMENT e3u: E3-14's banner markers on maps (MapMark.name: a '## Protocol' line), then E3-15's particle and held-item groups. E3-14's optional map-frames runs in e3z.

groups.prompt: Track E3 group map-banners: build track-e3.md section E3-14 group map-banners. Commits: 1. Minecraft maps mark banners like vanilla. 2. Minecraft map banner markers show their names, friends too. Key points: needs E2's e2b merged (Held, MapStore::tick_carried_on and fill_in, MapMark, the held map picture); re-check the track-e2 anchors in the brief. (1) A typed MapBanner {pos, color, name} in maps.rs, read from and written to the codec's banners list (frames stays raw). MapStore::toggle_banner follows toggleBanner: in range -63..63 map pixels, a missing banner refused, the same banner removed, the 256 tracked limit, a banner_<color> marker at rotation 180. check_banners per filled column. Loading a map adds its markers. Using a filled map on a #minecraft:banners block in actions.rs toggles with the banner's colour and custom name; a refused toggle is a failed use. (2) MapMark.name: Option<String> (a line under '## Protocol' in the log; never bump PROTOCOL). The held map draws names with the GUI font, centred 4 map pixels below the marker at scale clamp(25/width, 0, 6/9) on a 0x80000000 background (MapRenderer.render). The owner's steps (the banner is renamed "Home" in the anvil: the fork's /give takes no custom_name component) and the kit line are in the brief.
